challenges.title: Show a 12-Month Revenue Trend
challenges.context: The CEO wants to see whether monthly revenue is rising, falling or seasonal across the last year.
challenges.prompt: Which primary visual best serves this decision?
options: Line chart with month on the x-axis and revenue on the y-axis
Pie chart with one slice per month
Single KPI card showing only the latest month
Scatter plot of month number versus row number
challenges.correctOption: Line chart with month on the x-axis and revenue on the y-axis
hints: The x-axis has a natural time order.
The decision depends on change over time.
A line chart makes trend and seasonality visible.
challenges.explanation: Line charts encode ordered time naturally and make direction, turning points and seasonality easier to see than part-to-whole charts.

challenges.title: Define the Retention KPI
challenges.context: A SaaS manager asks whether customers acquired in each month keep using the product over later months.
challenges.prompt: Which KPI design is most defensible?
options: Cohort retention: percentage of each acquisition cohort active in each later period
Total signups since company launch
Average employee age
Raw page views without a customer denominator
challenges.correctOption: Cohort retention: percentage of each acquisition cohort active in each later period
hints: The question is about behavior after acquisition.
Different acquisition months need comparable denominators.
Cohorts preserve the starting population for retention analysis.
challenges.explanation: Cohort retention compares like-with-like populations and prevents growth in new signups from hiding deterioration in existing-customer behavior.

challenges.title: Catch a Misleading Bar Chart
challenges.context: A dashboard shows product A at 98 satisfaction and product B at 96, but the bar-axis starts at 95 so A looks several times taller.
challenges.prompt: What is the main design risk?
options: The truncated axis exaggerates a small absolute difference
Bars can never display percentages
The chart needs more decorative colors
The data must be causal because it is visualized
challenges.correctOption: The truncated axis exaggerates a small absolute difference
hints: Compare the numeric difference with the visual difference.
Bar length is interpreted from a baseline.
Starting near 95 magnifies a two-point gap.
challenges.explanation: For bars, a zero baseline usually protects proportional interpretation. A truncated baseline can visually overstate small differences.

challenges.title: Design the Executive Landing Page
challenges.context: The CEO has five minutes each Monday. The analytics team currently shows 42 charts on one page.
options: Lead with a small set of decision KPIs and exceptions, then allow drill-down into diagnostic detail
Keep all 42 charts so no information is omitted
Replace all numbers with decorative gauges
Show raw transaction rows first
challenges.correctOption: Lead with a small set of decision KPIs and exceptions, then allow drill-down into diagnostic detail
hints: Executive attention is scarce.
The first page should answer what changed and where action is needed.
Details can exist behind drill-down rather than competing for attention.
challenges.explanation: A strong executive dashboard establishes hierarchy: headline outcomes, exceptions and actionable drivers first; diagnostic detail remains available without overwhelming the landing view.

challenges.title: Choose the Checkout KPI Set
challenges.context: E-commerce revenue fell. Product traffic is stable, so leadership wants to know whether checkout behavior changed.
challenges.prompt: Which KPI set best diagnoses the funnel?
options: Product view→cart rate, cart→checkout rate, checkout→purchase rate, plus counts at each stage
Only total website page views
Only total revenue
Employee headcount by office
Number of dashboard users
challenges.correctOption: Product view→cart rate, cart→checkout rate, checkout→purchase rate, plus counts at each stage
hints: A total outcome alone cannot locate the leaking stage.
Rates need their underlying counts for context.
Measure each transition in the funnel.
challenges.explanation: Stage counts plus transition rates identify where loss occurs and prevent a single top-line KPI from hiding the mechanism.

challenges.title: Model Orders with a Star Schema
challenges.context: An e-commerce model mixes customer attributes, order measures and monthly targets in one giant table, creating duplicate values and confusing filters.
options: Create fact tables at defined grains and dimensions for customer/date/product with one-to-many relationships
Keep duplicating customer attributes in every table and use many-to-many everywhere
Fix each visual separately with manual filters
challenges.correctOption: Create fact tables at defined grains and dimensions for customer/date/product with one-to-many relationships
hints: Start from business grain.
Dimensions describe; facts measure events.
Prefer a clean star schema.
challenges.explanation: A star schema makes grain and relationships explicit, reduces ambiguity and supports simpler measures.

challenges.title: Choose a DAX Measure
challenges.context: MRR must change dynamically when the user filters month, segment or plan.
options: A DAX measure that sums MRR in current filter context
A hard-coded text box
A calculated column that stores the grand total on every row
challenges.correctOption: A DAX measure that sums MRR in current filter context
hints: The value changes with slicers.
Measures respond to filter context.
Use a measure for a dynamic aggregate.
challenges.explanation: Dynamic report KPIs such as MRR generally belong in measures because measures recalculate under the current filter context.

challenges.title: Apply Filter Context with CALCULATE
challenges.context: Network leaders need on-time delivered shipments as a percentage of all delivered shipments while route/month slicers remain active.
challenges.prompt: Which DAX idea is central to the numerator?
options: CALCULATE a shipment count under an OnTime filter
Use Power Query to hard-code the current percentage
Duplicate every shipment row
challenges.correctOption: CALCULATE a shipment count under an OnTime filter
hints: The base measure is a count.
The numerator changes the filter condition.
CALCULATE modifies filter context.
challenges.explanation: CALCULATE evaluates an expression under modified filter context while preserving other relevant report filters.

challenges.title: Fix Broken Time Intelligence
challenges.context: The fact table skips dates with no visits and month-over-month measures behave inconsistently.
challenges.prompt: What is the strongest modeling fix?
options: Create a continuous date dimension and relate it to the fact table
Fill every missing date by duplicating a visit
Sort month names alphabetically
challenges.correctOption: Create a continuous date dimension and relate it to the fact table
hints: Facts do not always contain every date.
Time intelligence needs a stable calendar.
Use a date dimension.
challenges.explanation: A continuous date table provides consistent calendar context for filtering and time-intelligence measures.

challenges.title: Repair an Ambiguous Relationship
challenges.context: A model uses multiple bidirectional relationships and changing one slicer unexpectedly changes unrelated visuals.
challenges.prompt: What should the analyst do first?
options: Return to a clear star schema and use single-direction relationships unless bidirectional behavior is specifically required
Add more bidirectional relationships
Hide the slicer
challenges.correctOption: Return to a clear star schema and use single-direction relationships unless bidirectional behavior is specifically required
hints: Ambiguity often comes from the model.
More bidirectional paths can worsen it.
Simplify relationships and filter paths.
challenges.explanation: Simple one-to-many, single-direction relationships are easier to reason about and reduce ambiguous filter paths.

challenges.title: Design Regional Row-Level Security
challenges.context: Regional managers may see only their region; executives may see the complete portfolio.
challenges.prompt: Which control is designed for this?
options: Row-level security roles with validated user-to-region mapping
A hidden visual
Changing chart colors by region
challenges.correctOption: Row-level security roles with validated user-to-region mapping
hints: This is an access problem.
The restriction must apply to data rows.
Use RLS and test roles.
challenges.explanation: RLS applies data-access rules by user/role; it must be tested with representative identities before publication.

challenges.title: Speed Up a Slow Executive Report
challenges.context: An executive page contains 38 visuals, unused high-cardinality columns and complex measures. It takes many seconds to respond.
options: Reduce unnecessary visuals/columns, simplify the model and measures, then profile performance
Add more visuals so the load is parallel
Convert every field to text
challenges.correctOption: Reduce unnecessary visuals/columns, simplify the model and measures, then profile performance
hints: Performance begins with model and visual complexity.
Unused columns still cost memory.
Simplify first, then profile.
challenges.explanation: Lean models and focused report pages usually improve both usability and performance; profiling then identifies remaining bottlenecks.

challenges.title: Publish a Trusted BI Report
challenges.context: A dashboard is ready for leadership, but no one has reconciled it to source totals or tested the security roles.
challenges.prompt: What must happen before production publish?
options: Reconcile key metrics, test filters/refresh and RLS roles, and document definitions
Publish first and fix numbers if someone complains
Only rename the report
challenges.correctOption: Reconcile key metrics, test filters/refresh and RLS roles, and document definitions
hints: Publishing is a release process.
Numbers and access rules both need testing.
Reconcile, test and document.
challenges.explanation: A production BI report needs metric reconciliation, functional testing, security validation and documented definitions.
